description:
Upcoming passes of one satellite or several over a location within windowHours (default 48, or 72 with limit; up to 240), in time order and not ranked: limit 1 for "when is the next pass?", no limit for the full schedule ("when does it pass this week?"). Which pass tool: find_passes lists passes in time order, from the next one (limit 1) to every pass in the window; find_best_pass ranks them by rating, for one satellite or, with none named, from a scan of many ("what can I see tonight?"); get_radio_pass gives one pass's Doppler and tuning, the next one by default. chart:true also draws the first pass listed as a sky chart (the image get_pass_chart gives) in this same result, so one call answers when and where to look. For another pass's chart give its peak time to get_pass_chart; to check clouds give it to get_pass_weather.

With a list of up to 10 satellites the result is one combined schedule: each pass also names its satellite, and satellites has one entry per satellite (one that can't be found gets an error there; the others still answer). Duplicates are listed once, and limit counts passes across the whole list. One satellite, not in a list, puts satellite, noradId and url at the top.

mode "visual" (default) keeps only the part of each pass that can be seen by eye, so rise and set can fall mid-sky and the peak is the highest point of that part; mode "radio" keeps the whole pass above minElevation. Rise and set are where it crosses minElevation, not the horizon, so a higher minElevation gives shorter, fewer passes. In visual mode the cloud forecast for the place is folded into the ratings.

rating is the one seeksat.com shows. Visual mode: how much brighter than the faintest visible star for skyType the pass gets (headroomMag), a level lower for some forecast cloud and one bar for a cloudy forecast, up to 4 days ahead; at most Fair when the brightness is estimated, the peak is below 15 degrees or it is seen for under a minute, at most Good below 25 degrees or when seen for under 2 minutes, and Excellent only above 40 degrees. Radio mode: the peak height, a bar lower for each 6 dB of extra path loss beyond 2,000 km, and at most Fair when SatNOGS stations tried at least 3 times in 30 days and heard nothing.

An empty list comes with a note saying why (it never rises high enough from that latitude, the sky never gets dark, and so on); when the next pass is further off, give a longer windowHours. Each pass is about 1 KB. SeekSat keeps nothing between calls (no saved places, lists or alerts), so give the place every time; for a reminder, give the user passUrl, which opens the pass on seeksat.com, where Remind me alerts them before it starts. Read-only, free, no key needed; up to 120 requests per 60 seconds per IP address. A bad input or a failure comes back as an error result (isError) whose text names the problem and what to change. A place name is looked up with OpenStreetMap (one lookup a second, cached), which can add a few seconds; lat and lon or a grid square need none. Cloud forecasts are cached for 10 minutes per area. Over 72 hours (unless limit is 5 or less), with more than one satellite, or with chart:true it is a heavy call: one at a time per caller; another waits up to 20 seconds, then is refused as busy.

chart.description: true to also render the first pass's polar sky chart (PNG, 800 by 897 pixels, about 120 KB) and return it in this same result. Default false.

lat.description: observer latitude in decimal degrees, north positive (-90 to 90). Give it with lon, or give location instead.

limit.description: return only the first limit passes in time order, 1 to 100: 1 for the next pass. Default: every pass in the window.

location.description: where the observer is, when lat and lon are not given (they win when both are): a Maidenhead grid square (EN52, EN52ve, EN52ve12), coordinates in any common form ("41.88, -87.63", "41.88N 87.63W", "41°52'48"N 87°37'48"W", a Google Maps link or geo: URI), read locally, or a place name (city, address, landmark) looked up with OpenStreetMap.

lon.description: observer longitude in decimal degrees, east positive and west negative (-180 to 180).

minElevation.description: lowest elevation that counts: a pass must climb above it, and rise and set are when it crosses it, in degrees above the horizon (0 to 90). Default 10.

mode.description: "visual" (default): naked-eye passes, sunlit while the sky is dark; "radio": every line-of-sight pass, day or night.

satellite.description: NORAD catalog number (as a number or a string) or a name, e.g. 25544, "25544" or "iss"; or a list of up to 10, e.g. [25544, 48274], for one schedule of all their passes.

skyType.description: how dark the observer's sky is, for the visual rating as on seeksat.com: "city" (stars to magnitude 3.5), "suburban" (stars to magnitude 4.5), "rural" (stars to magnitude 5.5), "dark" (stars to magnitude 6.5). Default "suburban".

windowHours.description: how far ahead to look, in hours, up to 240 (10 days). Default 48, or 72 with limit.
